title: Externally observable structured evidence families for hypothesis reduction
question: Which fixed-cost action-conditioned evidence family provides the highest verified hypothesis-disambiguation efficiency without access to target identity or evaluator-only information?
hypothesis: Structured externally observable evidence can provide greater downstream-disambiguation utility per environment execution cost than independent scalar probes; an instrumented activation trace is retained only as an explicit non-deployable information ceiling.

arms.name: scalar_output
arms.intervention: one input row -> one binary output

arms.name: paired_output
arms.intervention: one input row plus one fixed single-bit counterfactual perturbation -> ordered pair of binary outputs

arms.name: quad_output
arms.intervention: four fixed input rows forming a predetermined one-bit neighborhood -> four binary outputs

arms.name: activation_trace_ceiling
arms.intervention: one input row -> ordered internal activation vector in the instrumented sandbox

endpoints.name: information_gain_per_environment_work
endpoints.role: primary — deterministic mutual information in bits divided by expected environment execution/read cost

endpoints.name: expected_remaining_candidates
endpoints.role: secondary — expected compatible hypothesis-set size after the action

endpoints.name: verified_candidate_budget_success
endpoints.role: secondary — downstream exact-verifier success at fixed B=8 where defined

endpoints.name: amortized_total_work
endpoints.role: secondary — environment work plus explicit candidate cache and selector work

held_constant: same 512-program static evaluation library per seed
same train/evaluation structure and truth disjointness

fixed_counterfactual.rule: for each legal base row x, x xor delta is paired with x; no delta selection occurs at evaluation

cost_model.candidate_cache_and_selector_cost: reported separately and amortized; never omitted from secondary total-cost accounting

leakage_rules: The action selector may use only candidate-predicted evidence for legal actions and the current candidate set.
Target identity/index is never an input to selection.
Target observations are revealed only after action selection.
No held-out verifier labels are supplied to the selector.
The fixed perturbation is determined before measurement and is identical across arms.
No confirmatory result is used to choose an evidence family.

decision_rule.condition: A deployable external channel exceeds scalar_output on the primary endpoint with a seed-level interval excluding zero.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that the registered structured external evidence family is more information-efficient on this finite workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: learned autonomous probe selection or general multimodal reasoning.

decision_rule.condition: activation_trace_ceiling wins but all external channels do not.
decision_rule.licenses: internal structured evidence is informative but deployable external evidence remains limiting.
decision_rule.does_not_license: access to internal state in arbitrary environments.

decision_rule.condition: raw information gain improves but downstream verification does not.
decision_rule.licenses: the evidence is informative but not aligned with useful computation.

schedule.note: Exact one-step channel characterization; no learned optimization.
